implementation_details.before: ARMED_CRUISING called setESCThrottle inside handleCruisingThrottle and again after the state switch
implementation_details.after: handleCruisingThrottle only evaluates cruise disengagement; the common epilogue sends finalPwm once
implementation_details.timing_and_placement: 20 ms throttle period, task priority 3, pinned to core 0
implementation_details.review_note: The bench had no ESC, so physical CAN traffic reduction was not measured with a receiver; the call-count reduction is deterministic from the control path and the dry-cruise branch completed safely.

implementation_details.timing_and_placement: ESP32-S3 remains at 240 MHz; framework remains Arduino plus ESP-IDF on espressif32 6.13.0
implementation_details.review_note: Assertions remain enabled at level 2 and C++ exceptions remain enabled. CONFIG_FREERTOS_TASK_FUNCTION_WRAPPER is no longer set. The HIL branch inherits OPENPPG_PERF_INSTRUMENTATION and must not be merged wholesale.

implementation_details.before: Altitude, temperature, and pressure consumers could trigger separate forced conversions, producing about 50 conversions per second
implementation_details.after: One task calls bmp.performReading every 40 ms and publishes altitude, absolute altitude, temperature, pressure, vertical speed, and a timestamp
implementation_details.timing_and_placement: Barometer task: 3072-byte stack, priority 1, core 1; I2C mutex timeout 20 ms; BMP3 ODR 25 Hz, temperature 2x, pressure 4x, IIR coefficient 15
implementation_details.review_note: Individual 32-bit float loads/stores are naturally aligned on ESP32-S3, but the fields are not published as one atomic C++ snapshot. A sequence counter, critical section, or queue-backed snapshot would make cross-core coherence explicit. Stack high-water marks were not captured.

implementation_details.before: vTaskDelayUntil could immediately run catch-up iterations after a missed period
implementation_details.after: UI and barometer reset lastWake to the current tick when one full period has already been missed
implementation_details.timing_and_placement: UI: 33 ms, priority 2, core 1; barometer: 40 ms, priority 1, core 1; BLE notify: 20 ms, priority 1, core 1
implementation_details.review_note: This intentionally drops stale work instead of preserving every nominal slot. It improves fairness but changes overload semantics and should be retained as a deliberate scheduling policy.

implementation_details.before: Arduino ST7735 path performed synchronous register/FIFO writes under an application SPI mutex
implementation_details.after: esp_lcd queues RGB565 color transfers on SPI3_HOST and calls lv_display_flush_ready from the transfer-complete callback
implementation_details.timing_and_placement: 32 MHz SPI mode 0; 8-bit command and parameter widths; queue depth 2; SPI_DMA_CH_AUTO; two DMA_ATTR buffers of 20,480 bytes each; bus max transfer 40,960 bytes
implementation_details.review_note: RGB565 bytes are swapped in CPU before queueing. A single pendingDisplay pointer allows one outstanding LVGL color transfer, so the second buffer overlaps rendering with transfer but does not create two simultaneous queued LVGL flushes.

implementation_details.before: The first native transport used spi_device_polling_transmit while display DMA could already be queued
implementation_details.after: spi_device_transmit routes MCP2515 traffic through the ESP-IDF device scheduler; receive SIDH through D7 is read as one 13-byte burst
implementation_details.timing_and_placement: 10 MHz SPI mode 0; device queue size 2; maximum register payload 16 bytes; MCP2515 clock default 16 MHz
implementation_details.review_note: This exact polling/queued mismatch caused the reproducible assertion. ESP-IDF invokes the display completion callback from SPI interrupt context; its bundled LVGL example also signals flush-ready there. Project callback/task synchronization still relies on volatile state and naturally atomic word access, so document or strengthen memory ordering before fleet release.

implementation_details.before: Two 20,480-byte half-screen RGB565 buffers were allocated although the synchronous flush could not overlap render and transfer
implementation_details.after: One buffer is passed to LVGL and the second 20,480-byte static allocation is removed
implementation_details.timing_and_placement: 160 x 128 x 2 bytes per full screen; each partial buffer holds half a screen
implementation_details.review_note: Correct only for the synchronous transport. P5 deliberately restores two DMA-capable buffers, so P5 and P7 are alternative display architectures.
